content:
# User thesis project (keywords: essay, thesis, NVivo, film scripts, Montserrat, Greg, Carla)

Status as of 2024-04-05 (from user messages, not verified):
- Using NVivo, installed 2024-04-03 on Greg's suggestion. User reports coding is going smoothly (claims ~30% faster; not verified).
- Coding film scripts into nodes: gender roles, power dynamics.
- Essay topic finalized: "Representation of Women in Film," 1990-2020, "Montserrat cinema". Ambiguous: Montserrat (Caribbean territory, very little film output) vs Montserrat (Catalonia). Asked user to clarify; not yet answered.
- Carla reviewed an April 1 outline at Café La Belle; user worries thesis clarity is weak. The outline was NOT uploaded (uploads dir empty). Asked user to paste it.
- Deadline unknown; asked user for it. Do not impose timelines.
- 2024-04-05: User inspired by Robert's 1985 essay on gender studies shared on April 4 Zoom call. Essay not uploaded; citation details unknown. Asked about avoiding plagiarism of his ideas. User also said they'd share a "revised thesis" with Carla, but none was shown to me; I had only given a checklist.
- 2024-05-10: User confirmed first draft due May 15, 2024, 4,500 words. User asked for help managing time to finish the draft. Still open: Montserrat clarification, outline never uploaded, Michele's rubric, Robert's essay citation. Gave ordered steps without hour estimates.
- 2024-05-10: User attended Michele's 6 PM workshop May 8, MCC Room 204, on integrating counterarguments. User asked how to apply it. Workshop content not shared with me beyond the topic; asked for her notes.
- 2024-05-10: User says Heather gave feedback on May 7 via Google Docs asking for more statistical evidence. Heather's comment and draft not shared with me. Asked for them.
- 2024-05-10 preference (user instruction): when the user asks about draft revisions, recommend using Scrivener's split-screen mode for editing. User uses Scrivener since May 5 and prefers split-screen for note-taking.
- 2024-05-10: User says Robert reviewed the draft May 9 and recommended stronger warrants for gender-bias claims. Robert's comments not shared with me. User asked whether to prioritise this over other revisions.
- 2024-05-10: User replaced 2 weak sources with 3 peer-reviewed articles found May 6; asked about grade impact. Also: user has 4,200 words as of May 9. Shannon raised concern May 8 about late-night editing; user agreed to stop by 10 PM. Shannon's full concern not shared with me.
- 2024-06-01: User says Carla hosted a celebratory dinner at The Blue Lagoon on May 20 where they discussed "next research steps." Content of that discussion NOT shared with me; asked user for their notes. Essay grades due June 10.
- 2024-06-01: Deadlines: conference paper with Greg due June 3; essay to Montserrat Journal of Media Studies due June 5 (Robert recommended). User worried about both. Asked for prioritized schedule. Not yet verified: journal submission guidelines, conference paper requirements, whether journal accepts previously submitted class work.
- 2024-06-01: User aims for 90% grade and essay accepted for publication by August 2024. Note: the May 15 essay is already submitted, so its June 10 grade is fixed; 90% target now applies to revisions/publication version. Acceptance is decided by the journal's reviewers, not the user.
- 2024-06-01: User has a conference ABSTRACT deadline June 15 and is drafting an outline. Unclear whether this is the same conference as the June 3 paper with Greg; asked user to confirm.
- 2024-06-01: User decided to restructure essay into journal format and add a ~500-word literature review. User reports praise from Carla (May 20) and encouragement from Robert (June 1); not shared with me, unverified.
- 2024-06-01: User declined a $3,000 freelance project on May 25 to focus on the journal submission; feeling stuck and asked whether it was the right call. Reasons/finances not shared; no verdict given.
- 2024-06-01: Meeting with Greg moved from 3 PM to 5 PM on June 2 (production deadline on Greg's side). Conference paper due June 3. User asked how to manage time without burning out. Reminder: user agreed (May 8, via Shannon's concern) to stop editing by 10 PM.
- 2024-06-01: User planned qualitative interviews with 5 Montserrat filmmakers for August 2024; wants help preparing interview questions. Not yet checked: ethics/IRB approval, consent process, which Montserrat (Caribbean vs Catalonia) determines who counts as a filmmaker here.
- 2024-06-01: User now says interviews with 7 Montserrat filmmakers in August (earlier message said 5). Asked for a question list on gender portrayal. Still unresolved: which Montserrat; ethics approval; consent.
- 2024-06-01 user preference (instruction): always confirm submission dates when the user asks about deadlines. Open date questions: is the journal essay already submitted (5 days early = May 31?) or still due June 5; is the June 15 abstract the same conference as the June 3 paper with Greg.
- 2024-04-05: User says Michele rated the essay outline 82% on April 2. Target 90% on first draft due May 15 (user's stated deadline). Michele's feedback/rubric not shared with me; asked for it.
- 2024-07-15: User says the essay grade of 92% was received on July 10 (not July 15); praised for argumentation and evidence synthesis. User now feels confident and wants a progress review and conference-prep plan for the July 20 Zoom with Robert. No progress documents (draft, outline, abstract status) have been shared with me since June 1.
- 2024-07-15: User says the conference paper with Greg was submitted to the "Montserrat Media Symposium" on July 12. Conflicts with the June 3 paper deadline in my notes; unclear whether this is the same paper, a different venue, or a later round. User still refers to "our conference paper draft" and wants collaboration advice. Asked user to confirm venue, submission date, and whether revisions are still open.
- 2024-07-15: User says Carla recommended EndNote as a citation tool during a lunch at Café La Belle on July 5. Not in my earlier notes. User is writing in Scrivener. Asked how to get the most from EndNote; advice given on setup, Word plugin, and a Scrivener workflow. Verify EndNote version features on vendor site. Unclear which essay (May 15 draft or journal version). Next discussion with Robert on July 20 about next steps. Asked how to improve further. Unverified: the grader's written comments (not shared). Open items still relevant: Robert's May 9 request for stronger warrants on gender-bias claims; Heather's request for more statistical evidence; Montserrat (Caribbean vs Catalonia) still unclarified; ethics approval/consent for August filmmaker interviews still unchecked (5 vs 7 interviewees conflict).
- 2024-07-15: User reports Michele's July 8 workshop feedback shows a 40% improvement in rebuttal technique (unverified, feedback not shared). Plans conference paper editing July 16-18, though a July 12 submission was also reported. Asked how to apply rebuttal techniques; advised on concede/refute/reframe approach and asked for the feedback and paper status.
- 2024-07-15: User says conference paper has a FINAL submission deadline of July 20 and plans editing July 16-18 to make it 'perfect'. Conflicts with July 12 submission reported earlier (may be an initial submission). Also July 20 is the Zoom with Robert. Asked to confirm what July 20 requires; gave a priority order for July 16-18 (requirements/format first, then argument and rebuttals, then citations and figures, then proofreading).
- 2024-07-15: User feeling energized after 92% grade and 'positive peer reviews' (peer reviews not shared). Considering pursuing academic publishing full-time; unclear whether this means an academic career (research/teaching) or the publishing industry. Advised a decision framework (clarify the path, finances, funding/job market, alternatives, mentor input) and to raise it with Robert on July 20. No decision made by me; user's call.
- 2024-07-15: User decided to expand research to Caribbean-wide film representation after feedback on July 10 (feedback not shared; which feedback unclear). Implications flagged: conference paper final deadline July 20 and the Montserrat-specific design (NVivo coding, August interviews, ethics/consent not confirmed). Advised: keep current deliverables scoped to Montserrat, confirm the new direction with Robert/Carla, plan a separate phase with a revised sample, ethics amendment, and literature review. Montserrat (Caribbean vs Catalonia) still unclarified; Caribbean expansion seems to imply the Caribbean territory.
- 2024-07-15: User considering buying EndNote for $250 and says they trialed the 'free version' on July 6 (after Carla's July 5 recommendation). Note: EndNote is commercial; pricing and free-tier limits need checking on vendor site; university licences often free. Advised comparing against institutional access, free alternatives (Zotero, Mendeley, Word built-in), and the user's actual reference volume and workflow before buying.
- 2024-07-15: User declined a freelance offer on July 14 to balance a 35-hour work week with 10 hours of academic writing. Second declined freelance offer this summer (first: $3,000 project, May 25). Reasons and finances not shared. Asked whether it was the right decision; advised weighing finances, the pattern of declines, and whether the 10-hour writing block is protected in practice. No verdict given.
- 2024-07-15: User asked about EndNote 'improving citation insertion speed by 25%'. I did NOT say this; the figure did not come from me. Corrected the user. Any speed gain depends on their setup and should be measured on their own workflow.
- 2024-07-15: User adapted conference paper to Chicago style 'as required by the July 11 symposium' and asked for a format double-check. I do not have the paper or the symposium guidelines. Another date conflict (July 11 requirement vs July 12 submission vs July 20 final). Gave a Chicago checklist (notes-bibliography vs author-date, shortened notes, bibliography, quotations); asked for the guidelines and paper.
- 2024-07-15: User did a close reading of 3 new journal articles on Caribbean media on July 13 and asked to evaluate their approach. Approach/notes not shared (message ends with a stray fragment '->-> 5,14)'). Offered a critical-reading evaluation framework and asked for notes.
- 2024-07-15: User described close-reading approach for 3 Caribbean media articles (July 13): extensive annotation, section summaries, evidence evaluation, considered authors' perspectives, cross-article comparison of themes/differences. No notes shared. Gave specific feedback: summaries can replace evaluation; make evidence criteria explicit; examine positionality and silences; compare methods and sources, not just themes; use a claim-evidence-warrant table.
- 2024-07-15: User added 15 transition phrases to conference paper by July 14 and asked for connectivity tips. Paper not shared; message has stray fragment '->-> 5,15)'. Gave guidance: transitions should signal logical relations, avoid mechanical insertion, topic sentences/given-new/signposting; flagged that July 14 edits may postdate the July 12 submission. Asked for paragraphs.
- 2024-07-15: User prefers trialing writing software before buying; asked for options with free trials. Gave a categorized list (reference managers, writing/drafting, grammar/style, free tiers) with a caveat to verify trial terms on vendor sites. Note: user already uses Scrivener (since May 5) and NVivo; EndNote trial pending decision.
- 2024-07-15: User completed a 5-module online course on advanced argumentation by July 10 and asked how to apply it to essay writing. Course name, provider, and content not shared. Offered a general application plan (map course concepts to draft sections, test one claim per section, revise rebuttals, peer test) and asked for the syllabus or key takeaways.
- 2024-07-15: User used Hemingway Editor on July 15 and reports a 35% reduction in passive voice (figure not verified); asked if that is good enough. Answered: no fixed target; passive is appropriate in some places; check remaining passives for purpose; Hemingway flags are heuristic.
- 2024-07-15: User scheduled interviews with 3 Caribbean filmmakers for August 2024 fieldwork (previously 5, then 7 Montserrat filmmakers). Ethics approval and consent still unconfirmed. Advised confirming ethics approval/consent before any interview; gave an open-ended interview guide on gender representation, plus rapport and recording tips. Asked which territory the filmmakers are in.
- 2024-07-15: User feels confident about a conference presentation in September 2024 (venue not confirmed; may or may not be the Montserrat Media Symposium). Asked for strategies to maintain confidence. Gave preparation, rehearsal, Q&A, and recovery strategies; asked for venue and format.
- 2024-07-15: User took two full days off (July 13-14) to prevent burnout and is returning to the writing routine. Asked for motivation and burnout-prevention tips. Noted that earlier messages reported work on July 13-14 (close reading, transitions, freelance decline), so the days off may not have been fully off. Recalled the earlier agreement to stop editing by 10 PM (Shannon's concern). Gave routine, boundary, and early-warning tips.
- 2024-07-15: User says they are still waiting for grades on the essay submitted May 15, expects 90%+, and has never received academic grades or feedback before. CONTRADICTS earlier messages: user reported a 92% grade received July 10 (and peer reviews, Michele's July 8 feedback, Carla praise). Flagged the contradiction and asked which is correct. Offered anxiety-management guidance while waiting.
- 2024-07-15 user preference (instruction): when the user asks about new software or tools, always prioritize mentioning software trial periods (length, terms, what is included), verifying on vendor sites since I can't confirm them.
- 2024-07-15: User says conference paper editing extended through July 19 for late feedback; asks how this affects getting the essay published by August 2024. Journal submission status still unconfirmed. Advised: confirm journal status and review timeline; avoid parallel editing; check overlap between conference paper and journal version (prior-publication/duplicate disclosure rules); acceptance is reviewer-driven, so no promise.
